Since $\sqrt[5]{x}={x}^{1/5}$, we can apply the power rule with $n=\frac{1}{5}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{1/5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{1/5+1}}{(\frac{1}{5}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{6/5}}{(\frac{6}{5})}+C \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{6/5}}{6}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's check our answer by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{6/5}}{6}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{6/5}}{6})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{5}{6}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{6/5})+0 & = \\ \frac{5}{6}\cdot \frac{6}{5}{x}^{6/5-1} & = \\ {x}^{1/5}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
